questions.e:

보기 비교: improving(좋아지는)·recovering(회복하는)·advancing(나아지는)은 모두 긍정적인 변화라 '불행하게도'나 원인과 맞지 않는다.

기억 연결: deteriorate = get worse. Unfortunately + 나쁜 원인 → 부정적 변화.

Household Hazardous Waste
Leftover household products that can catch fire or explode under certain circumstances are considered household hazardous waste (HHW). Although it depends on your local solid waste agency or recycling facility, some examples include pesticides, paints, light bulbs, batteries, and nail polish. These products require special care when you dispose of them. HHW may be dangerous to people and bad for the environment if they are poured down the drain, dumped on the ground, or thrown out with regular trash.
What you can do:
▪Try to reduce your purchases of these products, and look for alternative, non-hazardous products.
▪When you need to dispose of these products, look for special collection events in your community or permanent collection centers.
▪If you have to dispose of HHW, first check with your local waste management agency to learn what rules apply in your community.

윗글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
c: ① to promote the safe disposal of HHW
② to show how HHW is managed at collection centers
③ to inform how to distinguish HHW from regular trash
④ to introduce local agencies dealing with HHW
questions.e:
정답 근거: 글은 가정용 유해 폐기물(HHW)이 무엇이고 잘못 버리면 사람과 환경에 해롭다는 점을 알린 뒤, 'What you can do'에서 구매 줄이기, 수거 행사·수거 센터 이용, 지역 기관의 규칙 확인 등 안전하게 처리하는 방법을 권한다. HHW의 안전한 처리를 장려하려는 ①이 목적이다.

보기 비교: ②의 수거 센터 안에서의 관리 방식, ③의 일반 쓰레기와 구별하는 방법, ④의 지역 기관 소개는 글의 목적이 아니다(기관은 규칙을 확인해 보라고만 했다).

기억 연결: 안내문의 목적은 마지막 행동 지침(What you can do)이 가장 잘 드러낸다.

문맥상 밑줄 친 regular의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
questions.e:
정답 근거: 'thrown out with regular trash'는 유해 폐기물을 '일반' 쓰레기와 함께 버리는 것을 말하므로 regular는 ordinary(보통의·일반적인)와 뜻이 가장 가깝다.

보기 비교: recyclable(재활용 가능한)·regional(지역의)·burnable(태울 수 있는)은 쓰레기와 어울리는 말이지만, 특별한 처리가 필요한 HHW와 대비되는 '보통의'라는 뜻이 아니다.

기억 연결: regular trash = ordinary household trash. 여기서 regular는 '규칙적인'이 아니라 '일반적인'.

Giraffes may all look identical to us. But none has exactly the same markings―and certain patterns, especially large, round patches, can boost their chances of survival before they turn 4 months old. Biologists can’t decide why giraffes evolved patches. David Lee at the Nature Institute in South Carolina and his colleagues examined 258 wild baby Masai giraffes in Tanzania for clues to the impact of patches on the animals. They found that calves with fewer, larger spots had a 17 percent higher chance of survival than those with more, smaller spots. They also found that those with more round spots had a 27 percent higher survival rate than those with elliptical* spots.
* elliptical: 타원형의
c: ① the unique ways to raise baby giraffes in Tanzania
② different survival rates of baby giraffes by region
③ the relationship between baby giraffes’ spots and survival rates
④ scientific methods to conduct research on giraffes’ calves
questions.e:
정답 근거: 연구진이 야생 마사이 기린 새끼 258마리를 조사해, 반점이 적고 큰 개체와 둥근 반점이 많은 개체의 생존율이 더 높다는 것을 발견했다. 새끼 기린의 반점과 생존율의 관계가 주제다.

보기 비교: ①의 새끼 기르는 방법, ②의 지역별 생존율 차이, ④의 연구 방법은 다루지 않는다(탄자니아는 조사 장소일 뿐이다).

기억 연결: 주제는 연구 결과 문장(They found that …)에 모인다.

questions.q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

In the face of significant education policy challenges such as emerging skills shortages and the need for teaching and learning innovation, schools are seeking ways to enhance school effectiveness.

(A) By assisting teachers to better understand student learning processes and education policies, schools can improve teacher effectiveness and address the looming teacher shortage resulting from retiring baby-boomers and staff who leave when their term contracts end.
(B) Schools should then effectively and efficiently convey this vital information to teachers in a way that maintains the teaching quality.
(C) To survive these shortages, schools must put processes in place before teachers leave and their pedagogical knowledge leaves with them. Because of the ageing workforce, it is critical to have effective succession planning in place to capture this knowledge.
questions.e:
정답 근거: 주어진 글은 학교들이 인력 부족 같은 과제 속에서 학교의 효과를 높일 방법을 찾는다고 한다. (A)는 교사의 이해를 도와 교사의 효과를 높이고 은퇴 등으로 인한 교사 부족에 대처할 수 있다고 하고, (C)가 'these shortages'를 받아 교사가 떠나기 전에 그들의 교수 지식을 붙잡는 승계 계획이 필요하다고 한다. (B)는 'then'과 'this vital information'으로 (C)에서 붙잡은 지식을 교사들에게 전하라고 마무리한다.

보기 비교: (B)의 'this vital information'과 'then'은 앞에 붙잡아 둔 정보가 있어야 하므로 (C) 뒤에 온다. (A) 바로 다음에 (B)가 오면 전할 정보가 무엇인지 앞에 없다.

기억 연결: 지시어(these shortages, this vital information)와 연결어(then)가 가리키는 말을 앞 단락에서 찾는다.

questions.q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

The gap probably had more to do with each school’s resources than with a student’s daily ration of chocolate cereal.

We’ve all heard that kids who eat breakfast do better in school. ( ① ) It makes sense; it’s hard to focus on an empty stomach. ( ② ) But despite their best attempts, researchers haven’t been able to pinpoint why breakfast aids learning―if that’s even the case. ( ③ ) A study of elementary school students found that, in some schools, kids behaved better after they ate breakfast; in other schools, they acted worse. ( ④ ) Students at well-equipped schools behave better regardless of their diet.
questions.e:
정답 근거: 주어진 문장의 'The gap'은 어떤 학교에서는 아침을 먹은 뒤 행동이 좋아지고 다른 학교에서는 나빠진 차이를 가리키고, 그 차이가 시리얼보다 학교의 자원과 관계가 있다고 한다. ④ 뒤의 '시설이 잘 갖춰진 학교의 학생들은 식단과 관계없이 행동이 더 좋다'가 이 설명을 이어받으므로 ④에 들어간다.

보기 비교: ①~③ 자리에서는 아직 학교 사이의 차이가 나오지 않아 'The gap'이 가리킬 대상이 없다.

기억 연결: 문장 넣기는 주어진 문장의 정관사·지시어(The gap)가 가리키는 내용이 바로 앞에 있는 자리를 찾는다.

Films, like literary works, are powerful instruments of education. ①On a simpler level, English language movies can be used in classrooms as a vehicle for teaching the English language. ②However, the animated film Future Galaxy deals with social issues from a historical perspective. ③But on a higher level, movies can be used as prisms through which one can learn how to understand, analyze and “read” complex aspects of the world humans have constructed and deconstructed in diverse issues in cultural, social, political, and economic spheres. ④Perhaps not most, but many Hollywood movies can be an insightful source to teach not only American culture, but also socio-economic-political-historical facets in content-based classes.
questions.e:
정답 근거: 글은 영화가 강력한 교육 도구라는 주제 아래 '단순한 수준(On a simpler level)'에서는 영어 교육, '더 높은 수준(But on a higher level)'에서는 복잡한 세계를 이해하는 도구라고 나누어 설명한다. 특정 애니메이션이 사회 문제를 역사적 관점에서 다룬다는 ②는 이 두 수준의 흐름을 끊는다.

보기 비교: ①과 ③은 'simpler level ↔ higher level'로 짝을 이루고, ④는 할리우드 영화가 미국 문화와 사회·경제·정치·역사적 측면을 가르치는 자료가 된다며 ③을 이어받는다.

기억 연결: On a simpler level … But on a higher level 사이에 끼어든 문장을 의심한다.

Recently, it has been demonstrated in a series of ingenious experiments that we even perceive colors through ______________________________________________. There are radical variations in the way languages carve up the spectrum of visible light; for example, green and blue are distinct colors in English but are considered shades of the same color in many languages. And it turns out that the colors that our language routinely obliges us to treat as distinct can refine our purely visual sensitivity to certain color differences in reality, so that our brains are trained to exaggerate the distance between shades of color if these have different names in our language. As strange as it may sound, our experience of a Chagall painting actually depends to some extent on whether our language has a word for blue.

Most of us put a lot of stock in what scientists tell us because we know that scientists reach their conclusions by gathering and analyzing facts. If someone asked you why you believe that smoking is bad and jogging is good, or that the earth is round and the galaxy is flat, you would point to the facts. You might need to explain that you do not personally know the facts to which you are pointing, but that you do know that at some time in the past, a bunch of very earnest people in white lab coats went out and watched the world, wrote down what they looked into, analyzed what they wrote down, and then told the rest of us what to believe. Scientists are credible because they draw conclusions from _____________, and ever since the empiricists trumped the dogmatists* and became the kings of ancient Greek medicine, westerners have had a special reverence for conclusions that are based on things they can see.
